sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>
sections.docs:
<docs>
Pi documentation (read only when the user asks about pi itself, its SDK, extensions, themes, skills, or TUI):
- Main documentation: /usr/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/README.md
- Additional docs: /usr/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs
- Examples: /usr/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/examples (extensions, custom tools, SDK)
- When reading pi docs or examples, resolve docs/... under Additional docs and examples/... under Examples, not the current working directory
- When asked about: extensions (docs/extensions.md, examples/extensions/), themes (docs/themes.md), skills (docs/skills.md), prompt templates (docs/prompt-templates.md), TUI components (docs/tui.md), keybindings (docs/keybindings.md), SDK integrations (docs/sdk.md), custom providers (docs/custom-provider.md), adding models (docs/models.md), pi packages (docs/packages.md), environment variables (docs/environment-variables.md), MCP servers (docs/mcp.md), codemode scripts and non-LLM models such as classifiers and image models (docs/codemode.md)
- When working on pi topics, read the docs and examples, and follow .md cross-references before implementing
- Always read pi .md files completely and follow links to related docs (e.g., tui.md for TUI API details)
</docs>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

content.text:
Implement the class `RollingMedian` in src/rolling-median.js, as a named export. The stub in that file shows the methods, and test/rolling-median.test.js shows two examples. Run the tests with: node --test. Do not change any file under test/.

Rules:
R1. `new RollingMedian(windowSize)` requires `windowSize` to be an integer of 1 or more; anything else throws a `RangeError`.
R2. `add(x)` requires `x` to be a finite number (not NaN, not an infinity, not a numeric string) and throws a `TypeError` otherwise, leaving the window unchanged. A valid `x` goes in as the newest value; if the window now holds more than `windowSize` values, the oldest value is dropped. `add` returns the median of the window after that.
R3. The median of the window is the middle value after sorting ascending. When the window holds an even number of values, it is the lower of the two middle values (not their average). `median()` returns the same thing at any time, and returns `null` when the window is empty.
R4. The getter `size` is the number of values currently in the window. `values()` returns a new array of the values from oldest to newest; changing that array does not change the window.
R5. `reset()` empties the window and returns `undefined`. The window size is kept.
R6. `resize(n)` sets a new window size, with the same check as R1. If the window holds more than `n` values it drops the oldest ones until it holds `n`. It returns the median after resizing (`null` if empty). Later calls to `add` use the new size.

When all the rules hold, reply with the single word: done

content.thinking: First, let's check the stub file and the test file.

Implement the class. Simple approach: keep the window as an array (in order from oldest to newest). For median, sort a copy. O(n log n) per add — for a simple implementation, that's fine.

R1: windowSize must be an integer >= 1, otherwise RangeError.
R2: add(x): x must be a finite number (typeof x === 'number' && Number.isFinite(x)), otherwise TypeError, window remains unchanged. Push x, and if length > windowSize, shift. Return the median.
R3: Median = sorted[Math.floor((n-1)/2)] — in the case of an even count, the lower of the two middle values: n even → indices (n/2 -1) and n/2; the lower is sorted[n/2 - 1]. floor((n-1)/2): n=2 → floor(0.5)=0 → sorted[0] ✓. n=4 → floor(1.5)=1 → sorted[1] ✓ (middle of 4 elements: indices 1 and 2, lower = 1). n odd: n=3 → floor(1)=1 ✓.
median() returns the same thing; if empty, null.
R4: size getter; values() returns a new array (copy).
R5: reset() clears and returns undefined. windowSize is preserved.
R6: resize(n) performs the same check as R1 (invalid n → RangeError). If it exceeds n values, drop from the oldest until it reaches n. Returns the median (null if empty).

Note: `resize(n)` — the R1 check requires that n be an integer greater than or equal to 1, and that it throw a RangeError for anything else. The `typeof n !== "number"` check excludes NaN and boolean values. Good.

Running the tests.

content.text:
Both tests pass. Implementation in src/rolling-median.js:

- **R1/R6**: shared `assertWindowSize` check (number, integer, ≥ 1, else `RangeError`) used by `constructor` and `resize`
- **R2**: `add` validates `typeof x === "number" && Number.isFinite(x)` before touching the window (else `TypeError`, unchanged), pushes newest, shifts oldest while over capacity
- **R3**: `median()` sorts a copy ascending and picks `sorted[Math.floor((n-1)/2)]` — the lower middle for even counts — or `null` when empty
- **R4**: `size` getter and `values()` returning a fresh copy
- **R5**: `reset()` clears the window, returns `undefined`, keeps `windowSize`
- **R6**: `resize` re-checks, trims oldest values to the new size, returns the new median

done
